tasks.description:
Implement in-memory `Store` with deterministic, collision-safe codes

Files:
- Create: `shortener/store.go`
- Create: `shortener/store_test.go`

Pattern: None. The sandbox repo has no existing code anchors (see Open Items).

Interfaces:
- Produces:
- `type Store struct`
- `func NewStore() *Store`
- `func (s *Store) Save(url string) string`
- `func (s *Store) Lookup(code string) (string, bool)`
- unexported `func deriveCode(url string, attempt int) string`
- unexported field `codeFn func(string, int) string`, defaulting to `deriveCode` so tests can force collisions
- Consumes: nothing.

Steps:
0. Baseline: `go version` reports 1.22 or later, and `go vet ./... && go test ./...` is green (or reports "no packages" on an empty repo). If not, stop and report.
1. Write `shortener/store_test.go` (package `shortener`) with these failing tests:
- `TestDeriveCode` (table): the same URL and attempt give the same result. The result has length 6 and only `[0-9A-Za-z]`. Attempt 0 differs from attempt 1 for the same URL.
- `TestSaveLookup`: `code := s.Save("https://example.com/a")` has length 6, and `Lookup(code)` returns the URL and `true`. `Lookup("zzzzzz")` returns `"", false`.
- `TestSaveIdempotent`: two `Save` calls with one URL return the same code (FR-4).
- `TestSaveCollision`: set `s.codeFn = func(u string, a int) string { if a == 0 { return "AAAAAA" }; return fmt.Sprintf("B%05d", a) }`. Then `c1 := s.Save("http://a")` and `c2 := s.Save("http://b")`. Assert `c1 != c2`, that each code looks up its own URL, and that a second `Save("http://b")` returns `c2`.
- `TestSaveConcurrent`: 50 goroutines call `Save` on a mix of identical and distinct URLs. Assert no panic, and that identical URLs got identical codes.
2. Run `go test ./shortener/...` and confirm a compile failure (undefined `NewStore`).
3. Implement `shortener/store.go`:
- `Store` has `mu sync.RWMutex`, `byCode map[string]string`, `byURL map[string]string` and `codeFn`.
- `deriveCode(url, attempt)` hashes `url` when `attempt == 0`, or `url + strconv.Itoa(attempt)` otherwise, with `crypto/sha256`. It converts the digest with `new(big.Int).SetBytes(sum[:]).Text(62)` and returns the first 6 characters.
- `Save` takes the write lock. If `byURL[url]` exists it returns that code. Otherwise it loops `attempt := 0; ; attempt++`. It computes `code := s.codeFn(url, attempt)`, and if `byCode[code]` is absent it records both maps and returns. If the code is taken (necessarily by a different URL, since the same URL was already handled), it continues.
- `Lookup` takes the read lock.
4. Run `go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` and confirm green.
5. Commit: `git add shortener/store.go shortener/store_test.go && git commit -m "feat(shortener): add in-memory store with deterministic collision-safe codes"`

tasks.description:
Implement `ValidateURL`

Files:
- Create: `shortener/validate.go`
- Create: `shortener/validate_test.go`

Pattern: None (greenfield).

Interfaces:
- Produces: `func ValidateURL(raw string) error`. Error messages are exactly:
- `url is required`
- `url must be a valid http or https URL`
- `url must be at most 2048 characters`
- Consumes: nothing.

Steps:
1. Write `shortener/validate_test.go` (package `shortener`) with a table test `TestValidateURL`, which fails to compile before the implementation exists. Cases:

| Input | Result |
|-------|--------|
| `http://example.com` | ok |
| `https://example.com/a?b=c` | ok |
| `HTTP://EXAMPLE.COM` | ok |
| `""` | `url is required` |
| `ftp://example.com` | `url must be a valid http or https URL` |
| `javascript:alert(1)` | same |
| `//example.com` | same |
| `http://` (no host) | same |
| `not a url` | same |
| `"http://a.com/"` padded with `a` to exactly 2048 runes | ok |
| the same input padded to 2049 runes | `url must be at most 2048 characters` |

Assert on `err.Error()` for the failing cases.
2. Run `go test ./shortener/...` and confirm the failure.
3. Implement `shortener/validate.go`:
- Empty string returns the required error.
- `utf8.RuneCountInString(raw) > 2048` returns the length error. The length check runs before parsing.
- `net/url.Parse(raw)` failing, a scheme other than `http` or `https` (the parser lowercases the scheme), or an empty `Host` returns the invalid error.
4. Run `go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` and confirm green.
5. Commit: `git add shortener/validate.go shortener/validate_test.go && git commit -m "feat(shortener): add URL validation"`

tasks.description:
Add `cmd/shortener/main.go` with `PORT` override and graceful shutdown

Files:
- Create: `cmd/shortener/main.go`
- Create: `cmd/shortener/main_test.go`

Pattern: None (greenfield).

Interfaces:
- Produces: unexported `func listenAddr(getenv func(string) string) string`, and `func main()`.
- Consumes: `shortener.NewStore()` (T001) and `shortener.NewHandler(*Store)` (T003), imported from `github.com/mayank-kochava/coding-agent-sandbox/shortener`.

Steps:
1. Write `cmd/shortener/main_test.go` (package `main`) with table test `TestListenAddr`:
- `PORT` unset or empty gives `:8081`.
- `PORT=9090` gives `:9090`.
- Drive it with a fake `getenv` closure.
2. Run `go test ./cmd/...` and confirm the failure.
3. Implement `main.go`:
- `listenAddr` returns `":" + p` when `getenv("PORT")` is non-empty, else `":8081"`.
- `main` builds `srv := &http.Server{Addr: listenAddr(os.Getenv), Handler: shortener.NewHandler(shortener.NewStore()), ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second}`.
- It runs `ListenAndServe` in a goroutine.
- It waits on `signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)`.
- On signal it logs `shutting down`, calls `srv.Shutdown` with a 5-second timeout context, and exits 0. A `ListenAndServe` error other than `http.ErrServerClosed` is logged and exits 1.
4. Run `go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` and confirm green.
5. Runtime check:
```bash
go build -o /tmp/shortener ./cmd/shortener
PORT=8099 /tmp/shortener & PID=$!
sleep 1
curl -si localhost:8099/healthz      # expect HTTP/1.1 200 and body "ok"
kill -TERM $PID; wait $PID; echo $?  # expect "shutting down" logged and exit code 0
```
6. Commit: `git add cmd/shortener && git commit -m "feat(cmd): add shortener server with PORT override and graceful shutdown"`

Checkpoint: Slice US1 is runnable and healthy.

tasks.description:
Add `POST /shorten`

Files:
- Modify: `shortener/handler.go`
- Modify: `shortener/handler_test.go`

Pattern: Follow the `healthz` registration and handler-method style from T003.

Interfaces:
- Produces: `(h *handler) shorten`, registered as `"POST /shorten"` in `NewHandler`. The response shape is `{"code": string, "short_url": "/r/<code>"}`.
- Consumes: `ValidateURL` (T002), `(*Store).Save` (T001), `NewHandler` (T003).

Steps:
1. Add `TestShorten` to `handler_test.go` (a table of `POST /shorten` requests):

| Case | Expected |
|------|----------|
| `{"url":"https://example.com/a"}` | 201, `Content-Type: application/json`, `code` length 6, `short_url == "/r/"+code` |
| Same body sent twice | identical `code` both times (FR-4) |
| `{}` | 400, `{"error":"url is required"}` |
| `{"url":""}` | 400, `url is required` |
| `{"url":"ftp://x.com"}` | 400, `url must be a valid http or https URL` |
| URL of 2049 runes | 400, `url must be at most 2048 characters` |
| `not json` | 400, `{"error":"invalid request body"}` |
| `{"url":123}` | 400, `invalid request body` |
| Body of `{"url":"` + 1 MiB + 1 bytes of `a` + `"}` | 400, `{"error":"request body too large"}` |
| `GET /shorten` | 405 |

Error responses must also have `Content-Type: application/json`.
2. Run `go test ./shortener/...` and confirm the new cases fail (404 or 405).
3. Implement `shorten`:
- Wrap the body with `http.MaxBytesReader(w, r.Body, 1<<20)`.
- Decode into `struct{ URL string \`json:"url"\` }`.
- If the decode error satisfies `errors.As(err, new(*http.MaxBytesError))`, return 400 `request body too large`. Any other decode error returns 400 `invalid request body`.
- Call `ValidateURL`. On error, return 400 with `{"error": err.Error()}`.
- Otherwise call `h.store.Save`, then return 201 with `{"code": code, "short_url": "/r/" + code}`.
- Add a small `writeJSON(w, status, v)` helper.
4. Run `go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` and confirm green.
5. Runtime check: build and run as in T004, then:
```bash
curl -si -X POST localhost:8099/shorten -d '{"url":"https://example.com"}'
```
Expect 201 and a code, with the same code on a repeat call. Then send `-d '{}'` and expect 400.
6. Commit: `git add shortener && git commit -m "feat(shortener): add POST /shorten with validation and idempotent codes"`

Checkpoint: Slice US2 is fully functional and tested.

tasks.description:
Add `GET /r/{code}`

Files:
- Modify: `shortener/handler.go`
- Modify: `shortener/handler_test.go`

Pattern: Follow the handler-method style from T003 and T005.

Interfaces:
- Produces: `(h *handler) redirect`, registered as `"GET /r/{code}"`.
- Consumes: `(*Store).Lookup` (T001), `NewHandler` (T003). It reads `r.PathValue("code")`.

Steps:
1. Add `TestRedirect` to `handler_test.go`. Each case builds its own store, calls `store.Save` directly to seed it, and sends the request through `NewHandler(store)`:
- A saved URL `https://example.com/a?b=c&d=e` returns 302 with `Location` exactly equal to that URL (query string preserved).
- `GET /r/zzzzzz` (unknown) returns 404.
- `POST /r/anything` returns 405.
2. Run `go test ./shortener/...` and confirm failure.
3. Implement `redirect`. Look up `r.PathValue("code")`. If it is not found, return `http.Error(w, "not found", http.StatusNotFound)`. Otherwise set `w.Header().Set("Location", url)` and call `w.WriteHeader(http.StatusFound)`. Setting the header manually avoids any rewriting of the stored URL.
4. Run `go vet ./... && go test -race ./...` and confirm green.
5. Runtime check: with the binary running, shorten a URL, then `curl -si localhost:8099/r/<code>` should return 302 with the right `Location`. `curl -si localhost:8099/r/zzzzzz` should return 404.
6. Commit: `git add shortener && git commit -m "feat(shortener): add GET /r/{code} redirect"`

Checkpoint: Slice US3 is fully functional and tested. All FRs are met.
